status: DRAFT: every number and line here is a starting point. Verify against 2-3 sources and an engineer review before release.

chapters.title: The Goal
chapters.intro: Compression turns down the loud parts of a sound so the whole thing sits more evenly. How much, and how fast, decides whether it sounds punchy, smooth or squashed.
chapters.doThis: Play the busiest section of the track for about ten seconds. The Primer will check whether this track needs compression at all.
chapters.listenFor: How much the level jumps around. Notice which parts feel too loud and which get lost.

chapters.title: Ratio & Threshold
chapters.subtitle: How hard, and how often
chapters.intro: Threshold is the line where the compressor starts working. Ratio is how hard it pushes back once the sound crosses that line. Your goal already set the ratio to {ratio.start}:1, so you only need to ride the threshold.
chapters.doThis: Play the loudest part of the track. Slowly lower the threshold until the meter sits in the target zone on the loud parts.
chapters.tryThis: Flip between 2:1 and 8:1 for a few seconds to hear what ratio does, then come back to {ratio.start}:1.

chapters.title: Attack
chapters.intro: Attack is how fast the compressor grabs a sound once it gets loud. Slow attack lets the first hit of each note through. Fast attack catches it.
chapters.doThisFromFast: Start at {attack.start} ms. While the track plays, slowly turn Attack up. Stop when the start of each note pokes through the way your goal wants.
chapters.doThisFromSlow: Start at {attack.start} ms. While the track plays, slowly turn Attack down. Stop when the loud starts are under control.

chapters.title: Release
chapters.intro: Release is how fast the compressor lets go after the sound gets quieter. It should recover in time with the music, ready for the next note.
chapters.doThis: Start at {release.start} ms. Slowly turn Release down until the meter drops back toward zero before the next note or phrase hits.

chapters.title: Level & Compare
chapters.intro: Compression makes things quieter, and quieter always sounds worse. Match the level before you judge it.
chapters.doThis: Turn Makeup Gain until the output matches the original. Then hold Compare to flip between before and after at the same volume.
chapters.listenFor: Whether the after version does what you picked in Chapter I. If you can't tell them apart, that's fine for gentle goals.

chapters.title: Blend
chapters.intro: Parallel compression mixes a heavily squashed copy under the original. You keep the natural hits and add energy underneath.
chapters.doThis: Start Mix at 0%. Slowly bring it up while the drums play.

messages.listening: Keep playing. The Primer needs a few seconds of the loud part to take a reading.
messages.silence: Nothing is coming in. Press play on a section where this track is playing.

needCheck.needed: This track jumps around enough to benefit. Let's set it up.
needCheck.notNeeded: This track is already pretty even. Light settings or no compression at all may sound best. You can still continue.

ratioThreshold.low: Not catching enough yet. Lower the threshold until the meter sits in the zone on the loud parts.
ratioThreshold.high: That's more squeeze than this goal needs. Raise the threshold a little.
ratioThreshold.onTarget: That's the right amount of squeeze. Turn to Chapter III.

attack.low: Too fast. The front of each note is getting flattened. Turn Attack up.
attack.high: Too slow. The loud starts are slipping through untouched. Bring Attack down.
attack.onTarget: Right on target. Lock it in and turn to Chapter IV.

release.tooSlow: Too slow. The compressor never lets go before the next note. Shorten the release.
release.tooFast: Too fast. Release this short can make the sound flutter or distort. Lengthen it.
release.onTarget: The compressor is recovering in time with the music. Turn to Chapter V.

level.high: Louder than the original, which makes it sound better than it is. Turn Makeup down.
level.low: Quieter than the original. Add Makeup Gain until they match.
level.onTarget: Levels match. Now hold Compare and trust your ears.

blend.low: Barely any smash in there yet. Bring Mix up.
blend.high: The smash is taking over. Pull Mix back until the natural hits lead again.
blend.onTarget: That's the sweet spot: bigger and louder, still natural.

goals.name: More Punch
goals.tagline: Words hit harder and cut through

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Loud lines coming down a little so they stop jumping over the quiet ones.
listenFor.attack: T's, P's and K's popping forward while the body of each word stays controlled.
listenFor.release: The vocal relaxing back to full level between phrases, not hanging low.

goals.name: Smooth & Even
goals.tagline: Loud and quiet lines land closer together

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The big notes settling down to sit near the softer ones.
listenFor.attack: Loud syllables no longer jumping out. Too fast and the vocal starts to sound dull.
listenFor.release: A steady level line to line with no audible pumping.

goals.name: Upfront & Squashed
goals.tagline: Pinned in your face, modern rock style

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The vocal flattening into one solid level. This goal is supposed to sound heavy.
listenFor.attack: Every word pinned at the same level. Back off if the vocal turns lispy or crunchy.
listenFor.release: Dense and in your face. Breaths getting loud means release is too fast.

goals.name: Tuck Behind the Lead
goals.tagline: Steady parts that support without competing

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The backing parts holding one steady level under the lead.
listenFor.attack: The backing parts losing their sharp edges so they sit behind the lead.
listenFor.release: A steady bed with no swells between lines.

goals.name: Blend Together
goals.tagline: Several voices gel into one group (use on the vocal bus)

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Just a touch of movement on the meter. Glue is gentle.
listenFor.attack: The voices starting to sound like one group instead of separate singers.
listenFor.release: The group breathing with the song's tempo.

goals.name: Even Strumming
goals.tagline: Big strums and soft strums sit together

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The hardest strums coming down to meet the rest.
listenFor.attack: Loud strums no longer poking out while the strings keep their shimmer.
listenFor.release: A steady strum pattern with no dips after big hits.

goals.name: More Pick & Snap
goals.tagline: Crisper, more percussive playing

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The body of the guitar tightening up a little.
listenFor.attack: The pick hitting the strings getting crisper and more forward.
listenFor.release: The body of the guitar coming back up quickly between strums.

goals.name: Keep It Natural
goals.tagline: Barely there, just smooths the peaks

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The meter only flickering on the biggest moments.
listenFor.attack: Almost nothing. If you can clearly hear it working, it's too much.
listenFor.release: The guitar sounding like the raw take, just a little more consistent.

goals.name: Even & Sustained
goals.tagline: Notes ring longer and more evenly

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Picked notes and ringing notes landing at a similar level.
listenFor.attack: Notes ringing longer and more evenly. Too fast and the picking turns mushy.
listenFor.release: Sustain holding up without the tone swelling or breathing.

goals.name: More Pick Attack
goals.tagline: Snappier, more defined notes

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The ringing part of each note tightening slightly.
listenFor.attack: Each pick stroke getting snappier and more defined.
listenFor.release: The note body coming back up between pick strokes.

instruments.name: Electric Guitar (Distorted)
instruments.lesson: Distortion already squashes the sound, so heavy guitars usually need little or no compression. This goal teaches you to hear when to leave it alone.

goals.name: Light Touch
goals.tagline: A tiny bit of control, nothing more

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Barely any meter movement. That's correct here.
listenFor.attack: Very little change. Distortion already evens things out.
listenFor.release: No pumping. If you hear the guitar breathing, back everything off.

goals.name: Even Every Note
goals.tagline: Every note lands with the same weight

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Loud notes coming down so none of them jump out.
listenFor.attack: Every note landing at the same weight, low strings and high strings alike.
listenFor.release: Notes holding steady. Too fast and the low end starts to rattle or distort.

goals.name: Punchy & Defined
goals.tagline: A clear click at the start of each note

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The sustain of each note tightening up.
listenFor.attack: The pluck or pick getting a clear click at the start of each note.
listenFor.release: The bass bouncing back up in time with the groove.

goals.name: Thick & Locked
goals.tagline: A solid, unmoving wall of low end

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The bass flattening into one steady level.
listenFor.attack: A solid, unmoving wall of low end. Back off if notes lose definition.
listenFor.release: Thick and steady. Distortion on low notes means release is too fast.

goals.name: More Punch
goals.tagline: A sharper, louder beater click

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The boom after the hit getting slightly shorter.
listenFor.attack: The beater click getting louder and sharper.
listenFor.release: The compressor fully letting go before the next kick lands.

goals.name: More Body
goals.tagline: A bigger, rounder boom

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The hit and the boom moving closer together in level.
listenFor.attack: The click softening while the boom gets bigger after makeup gain.
listenFor.release: The tail of the kick growing longer and rounder.

goals.name: More Crack
goals.tagline: A sharper stick hit that cuts through

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The ring after the hit tightening up.
listenFor.attack: The stick hit getting sharper and cutting through more.
listenFor.release: The snare resetting fully between hits.

goals.name: Fatter
goals.tagline: More body and ring, less crack

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The hit coming down toward the body of the drum.
listenFor.attack: The crack softening and the body of the drum filling in.
listenFor.release: The ring and the snare wires coming forward.

goals.name: Glue
goals.tagline: The kit sounds like one instrument

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The meter moving a little on the biggest hits.
listenFor.attack: The kit sounding like one instrument instead of separate drums.
listenFor.release: The kit breathing in time with the groove. Off-time pumping means adjust release.

goals.name: Parallel Smash
goals.tagline: Crush a copy and blend it in for energy
goals.note: Chapters II to IV run with Mix forced to 100% so the user hears the smashed copy alone. Chapter VI (Blend) brings Mix down to taste.

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Lots of meter movement. Smashing is the point.
listenFor.attack: Slam it. On its own the smashed copy should sound wrecked, and that's expected.
listenFor.release: Room and cymbals swelling up between hits.
listenFor.blend: Bring the smash in until the kit feels bigger and more energetic, then pull back a touch.

goals.name: Even It Out
goals.tagline: Loud chords stop jumping over soft ones

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The loudest chords settling toward the rest.
listenFor.attack: Loud chords no longer jumping out over soft ones.
listenFor.release: Sustained chords staying natural, with no swelling.

goals.name: Keep It Natural
goals.tagline: Barely touched, performance intact

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The meter only touching the very loudest moments.
listenFor.attack: Barely there. The performance should feel untouched.
listenFor.release: No audible movement at all.

goals.name: Gentle Glue
goals.tagline: The whole mix gels together

listenFor.ratioThreshold: One or two dB on the loudest hits, no more.
listenFor.attack: The whole mix gelling together while the drums keep their hit.
listenFor.release: The mix moving with the tempo. If you can hear it pump, it's too much.

goals.name: Even & Clear
goals.tagline: Loud and quiet words land closer together

listenFor.ratioThreshold: Laughs and loud words coming down to conversation level.
listenFor.attack: Loud words and quiet words landing closer together.
listenFor.release: Steady level sentence to sentence without breaths popping up.

goals.name: Broadcast Steady
goals.tagline: That close, radio-host sound

listenFor.ratioThreshold: The voice locking into one steady level.
listenFor.attack: Every word at the same level, close and confident.
listenFor.release: Breaths and room noise getting loud between sentences means release is too fast.
